summary: NYU workshop paper (LMP @ EMNLP 2026) that post-trains Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with LoRA PPO-Lagrangian. The policy decides between asking a clarifying question and answering, maximising HumanEvalComm pass@1 subject to a budget on expected questions per episode, while a GPT-4o-mini oracle answers questions from the original spec. At a budget of 0.75 the trained policy (two seeds) asks fewer questions than the untrained model (0.72-0.78 vs 0.856) and passes more tests (+5.8 to +7.1 points). Budgets of 0.25 or below fall below baseline, and budgets above 1.0 add nothing.

claims.claim: Untuned clarification behaviour is Pareto-inefficient: a budget-constrained policy achieves higher accuracy with fewer questions.
claims.evidence: §5: d1=0.75 is the only budget that Pareto-dominates the baseline in both seeds (pass@1 +5.8 / +7.1 points, both p<0.01; question rate 0.719 / 0.782 vs 0.856, both p<0.01; paired t-tests on 417 held-out instances split by base problem). The only comparator is the same model untrained; there is no prompted 'ask only when needed' baseline and no penalty-based RL baseline, although the paper motivates itself against penalty methods.

claims.claim: The accuracy-clarification frontier is log-shaped with diminishing returns.
claims.evidence: Fig. 1 fits a log curve through five budget levels (two seeds only at 0.5/0.75/1.0); above 1.0 the multiplier is slack and pass@1 is flat. Authors acknowledge the interpolation between budgets is unverified, and one d1=1.0 run violates its budget at test time.

claims.claim: Gains come from better question targeting and code generation, not from asking more.
claims.evidence: 1Q->1Q episodes: +7.1 points (p<0.001, n=490). But App. C shows zero-question episodes also improve (73.7 -> 81.1% at d1=1.0), slack-budget runs with lambda about 0 also improve, and the Limitations section concedes question quality and code quality are not disentangled. Better code from PPO on HumanEval-family tasks explains part of the gain.

claims.claim: Trained policies allocate more questions to harder multi-degradation tasks without supervision.
claims.evidence: Fig. 2 and Fig. 6 descriptive breakdowns with SEM bars; no test against the baseline's own allocation; small cells (e.g. 3acp) flagged by the authors.

patterns.note: On synthetic HumanEval degradations with one 7B model, training clarification toward zero (d1 <= 0.25) fell below the untrained baseline, while a budget of about 0.75 questions per task Pareto-dominated it, so targeted asking helps and suppressing it hurts in this setting. The comparison is only against the untrained model (no prompted or penalty-RL alternative), and the user is a GPT-4o-mini oracle that answers from the full spec.

PPO-Lagrangian LoRA post-training beats the untrained model, but slack-budget runs (lambda about 0) also gain, so much of the improvement is generic PPO on HumanEval-family tasks. Seed variance is notable (0.683 vs 0.719 at d1=0.5) and there is no penalty-based RL baseline.
Expected question-count budget enforced by a Lagrange multiplier during training only; at evaluation the policy runs free and compliance is checked post hoc (d1=0.25 and one d1=1.0 run violate it).

methodology.sample: HumanEvalComm: 772 degraded instances; 303 train (64 base problems), 52 validation, 417 held-out test, with all variants of a base problem kept in one split; 7 degradation types.
methodology.baselines: Untrained Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct under identical multi-turn protocol only.
methodology.models: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (LoRA r=16) as policy; GPT-4o-mini (temperature 0) as user simulator.
methodology.variance: Two seeds at d1 in {0.5, 0.75, 1.0}, one seed elsewhere; paired t-tests and SEM bars; run-to-run differences acknowledged.
methodology.ablations: Budget sweep over 7 levels; slack-budget runs as an approximate unconstrained-PPO control; no frozen-code-head ablation.
methodology.contamination_controls: Split by base problem prevents train/test leakage; HumanEval pretraining exposure for Qwen2.5-Coder not discussed.

standards.peer_review: Accepted to the LMP Workshop at EMNLP 2026 (arXiv comment).
standards.artifacts: Code and trained checkpoints on GitHub (github.com/Abhinav0710rajput/coding_llms_cmdp).

biases.detail: HumanEval functions with synthetic ambiguity, inconsistency and truncation degradations.
Only the untrained model is compared; no prompted selective-clarification or penalty-RL baselines.
HumanEval is likely in Qwen2.5-Coder pretraining; not addressed.
Training pool of 303 instances from 64 base problems; two seeds at three budgets.
Deterministic GPT-4o-mini oracle with full-spec access stands in for human answers.

coi.affiliations: Center for Data Science, New York University.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Qwen2.5-Coder (open weights), GPT-4o-mini as simulator; no affiliation.

verdict_reason: Clean held-out split, two seeds with paired tests, honest limitations and released code and checkpoints support the narrow claim that one budget-trained 7B policy dominates its untrained self on HumanEvalComm. The comparator is weak, the setting is toy and simulated, and the 'better targeting' explanation is not isolated.
applicability: The method does not transfer: the team does not post-train models, since model choice belongs to the agent host and qr stays off the LLM path. Two directional signals are worth a harness default, both untested beyond HumanEval with a simulated user. Never asking hurt. Returns flattened after about one targeted question per ambiguous task. A pre-spec clarification step could therefore start with a small blocking-question budget (one or two questions per ticket, with further questions deferred into a written open-questions list) rather than unbounded questioning, and measure on the team's own tickets whether more questions pay off.
